newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA IN HISTORIC TROPHY WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA IN HISTORIC TROPHY WIN.

text.p: Vicenza beat a 10-man Napoli 3-0 after extra time and with a penalty shoot-out looming on Thursday to win the Italian Cup and shed their 95-year reputation as a team that never wins anything.

"We are deliriously happy," said Vicenza coach Francesco Guidolin, after the 3-1 aggregate win gave Vicenza their first trophy since their foundation in 1902 and a place in next season's European Cup Winners' Cup tournament.
The provincial club, without big name stars, could previously only boast having finished runners-up in the league in 1978 when Italian striker Paolo Rossi was on song.
On Thursday they found another Rossi to thank for their win at the antiquated Romeo Menti stadium.

Midfielder Maurizio Rossi, a substitute who came on in the first half of extra time, scored in the 117th minute with the score 1-1 on aggregate after Vicenza's Gianpiero Maini had cancelled out Napoli's 1-0 first leg advantage in the 20th.
The vital goal came when Napoli's French midfielder Alain Boghossian gave away a free kick on the edge of the area.
Goalkeeper Giusepe Taglialatela was unable to hold the shot and Rossi pounced at the far post for the rebound.
Alessandro Iannuzzi made it 3-0 almost on the whistle with another shot that slipped past Taglialatela.
"I coach a team of heroes," said Guidolin, who said he wanted to take time to savour the win and consider his future -- not necessarily at the small town club.
"They may be simple heroes, but they are heroes. The merit is all theirs. I didn't do anything," he said.
Vicenza's only previous appearance in Europe was in the UEFA Cup in 1979 when they lost to Dukla Prague in the first round.

Thursday's victory produced an explosion of celebration from the home crowd and violence from the small contingent of Napoli fans, who had hurled red flares and fireworks directly at the Vicenza supporters throughout the match.
Helmeted riot-police baton-charged the Napoli end as fighting broke out after the final whistle.
The violence had been feared, with the match carrying strong racist overtones in a clash between clubs from north and south.

Banners and slogans supporting the separatist Northern League were in evidence, including one comparing the southern port of Naples unfavourably with the Albanian capital Tirana and another saying "No to immigration".

Napoli, who had won the first leg 1-0 in Naples, looked doomed when striker Nicola Caccia was sent off in the second minute of extra time after apparently elbowing midfielder Fabio Viviani in the face while breaking down the wing.
Caccia had hit the bar in the second half.
Napoli coach Vincenzo Montefusco was then sent off the bench in the second period as tempers flared.
Montefusco said later he had sworn about the refereeing but refused to comment on Caccia's sending off. He also cast a blind eye on the flares, saying he saw nothing.
"I am just sorry that we couldn't at least make it to penalties," said the coach, who replaced sacked Luigi Simoni after struggling Napoli had reached the final.
"I think penalties would have been the fairest outcome, even if we had lost on them," Montefusco said.
Teams:

Vicenza - 22-Pierluigi Brivio; 2-Luigi Sartor, 10-Fabio Viviani, 6-Giovanni Lopez, 16-Massimo Beghetto, 25-Giuliano Gentilini (7-Maurizio Rossi 97), 4-Domenico Di Carlo, 13-Gianpiero Maini, 23-Gabriele Ambrosetti (15-Alessandro Iannuzzi 18), 9-Roberto Murgita, 11-Giovanni Cornacchini (3-Gilberto D'Ignazio 67)

Napoli - 1-Giuseppe Taglialatela; 5-Alain Boghossian, 2-Roberto Ayala, 15-Francesco Baldini, 3-Mauro Milanese, 22-Bertrand Crasson (13-Luigi Panarelli 97), 4-Roberto Bordin (14-Alfredo Aglietti 61), 23-Raffaele Longo (24-Luca Altomare 67), 9-Massimiliano Esposito, 11-Fabio Pecchia, 18-Nicola Caccia.
